reason: The cited evidence supports that Al and Cr can form protective oxides (E2, E4) and that a dense composite oxide can block oxidation (E3), but it does not directly support the specific claims about slower diffusion rates of Al/Cr relative to Mn or the direct link between Al/Cr enrichment and thinner scales; E1 is a general statement and E2 notes Cr2O3 was not detected in one study, which partially conflicts with the premise of its protective role.
premises: Selective oxidation of Al and Cr forms a protective oxide scale in HEAs.
The resulting oxide scale (e.g., Al2O3/Cr2O3 composite) physically blocks oxygen ingress and metal cation diffusion.
Al and Cr have higher oxygen affinity and slower diffusion rates than other elements like Mn.
A dense, multi-component oxide layer preserves bulk alloy composition and provides long-term oxidation resistance.
Increasing Al/Cr relative to Mn leads to thinner, more uniform, slower-growing oxide scales.
